t: You're on Prince Albert Road, a street that runs between the City of Westminster and the London Borough of Camden. It's named after Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, the husband of Queen Victoria. He was consort from their marriage on the tenth of February 1840 until his death in 1861, and Victoria granted him the title Prince Consort in 1857. So the road carries the name of the man at the centre of Victorian royal life.
